strengths: Well-motivated approach addressing genuine limitations of CVaR-PG (sample inefficiency, blindness to success, vanishing gradients with flat-tailed returns)
Solid theoretical contributions including new Bellman operator for VaR with contraction mapping properties and recovery of Markovian policies via cumulative reward tracking
Consistent empirical improvements across three test domains, with particularly clear benefits in Maze where CVaR-PG fails
Comprehensive baseline comparisons (CVaR-PG, PCVaR-PG, RET-CAP, MIX) with fair on-policy implementation
Principled handling of practical challenges (quantile crossing) with softplus-based monotonicity enforcement
Clear problem motivation and intuitive core idea grounded in CVaR's relationship to quantiles
weaknesses: Critical convergence gap: convergence properties under iterative updates from arbitrary initialization remain unknown; Proposition 3.4 only shows π* maximizes objective under corresponding value function, not during optimization
Theory-practice mismatch: theoretical results require ε=0, κ=0, but practical algorithm uses soft loss with ε,κ>0; applicability of theory to implementation unclear
Artificial experimental domains designed specifically to have verifiable risk-averse behavior; authors acknowledge environment design is itself a nontrivial problem; limited generalization assessment

Hyperparameter sensitivity and tuning burden: trade-off parameter ω is crucial but no ablation studies provided; domain-specific decay schedules suggest sensitivity without principled selection guidance
Incremental improvements over RET-CAP in some domains (LunarLander: 'slightly higher'); gains not consistently substantial despite added complexity
Missing ablation studies: no analysis of CVaR-PG (g₁) vs VaR-PG (g₂) component contributions; no failure mode analysis; limited investigation of when method excels
Experimental design concerns: implementations differ from original papers (on-policy without IS), only 10 seeds, no statistical significance tests; harder to assess true improvements
Limited algorithmic novelty: VaR Bellman operator closely follows Hau et al. (2025); main contribution is combination rather than novel components
Reproducibility limitations: domain-specific hyperparameters (ω decay schedules), no code mentioned, non-standard implementation choices
Presentation could be clearer: dense notation in Section 3.2, relationship between Algorithms 2-3 unclear, interaction of gradient terms g₁ and g₂ not deeply analyzed
